## Anatomy

- `root`: A `<code>`, or for a block a `<pre>` with the `<code>` inside.
- `text`: The `<code>` inside a block.

## When to use

- **A name in a sentence.** A prop, a token path or a file name inside running text: `tone=quiet`, `contracts/link.contract.yaml`.
- **What to write.** A few lines someone will copy. Coloured by a highlighter, or plain.

## When not to use

- **Emphasis.** Making a word stand out. Code means the word is exactly what you type.
- **Very long files.** A whole file on a page. Show the part that matters, and link to the rest.

## Behaviour

In a sentence it's the mono family at a slightly smaller size, with no plate, so a line full of token paths stays calm. A block gets the secondary plate, 16px inside and 12px corners, and scrolls sideways rather than wrapping.

The colours inside a block come from the highlighter, not from Rost. On the Rost site that's Shiki's vesper in dark and GitHub's high-contrast theme in light, with the comment greys made solid, so every word is 4.5:1 on the plate. Syntax colours as tokens would be the next step, and I haven't needed them in an app yet.

## Accessibility

- **Element**: `<code>`, and `<pre>` around it for a block, so a screen reader keeps the spacing.
- **Keyboard**: A block that scrolls gets `tabindex="0"`, so it can be scrolled without a mouse.

## Content

Exactly what someone types. No ellipsis inside a line they'd copy.

## No token, on purpose

| Part | Property | Value | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `root` | `font-family` | `'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, Menlo, monospace` | Rost has no mono family token yet. Where JetBrains Mono isn't loaded, the system mono stands in. |
| `root` | `font-size` | `0.88em` | In a sentence it follows the text around it. Mono looks bigger than General Sans at the same size, so a little smaller. |

See it live, with every value of every variant: [rost.build/components/code](https://rost.build/components/code/)
